name: Pantoprazole
uses: Acid reflux (GERD), heartburn, stomach ulcers.
side_effects: Headache, diarrhea, nausea, gas. Long-term use may lower magnesium and vitamin B12 and raise fracture risk.
extra_information: A proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) that reduces stomach acid. Usually taken before a meal as directed; prolonged use may require review for magnesium, vitamin B12, or bone-related risks. General note: these medicines are for specific digestive symptoms and are not interchangeable. Persistent symptoms, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools need medical assessment.

name: Omeprazole
uses: Acid reflux, heartburn, stomach and duodenal ulcers.
side_effects: Headache, stomach pain, diarrhea, nausea. Long-term use may lower magnesium and vitamin B12.
extra_information: A proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) that reduces stomach acid. Check with a clinician or pharmacist for interactions, including with clopidogrel; long-term use should be periodically reviewed. General note: these medicines are for specific digestive symptoms and are not interchangeable. Persistent symptoms, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools need medical assessment.

name: Esomeprazole
uses: Acid reflux (GERD), erosive esophagitis, ulcers.
side_effects: Headache, diarrhea, nausea, gas. Long-term use may lower magnesium and vitamin B12.
extra_information: A proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) that reduces stomach acid. Often taken before food; persistent symptoms or long-term use should be reviewed by a healthcare professional. General note: these medicines are for specific digestive symptoms and are not interchangeable. Persistent symptoms, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools need medical assessment.

name: Rabeprazole
uses: Acid reflux, ulcers, heartburn.
side_effects: Headache, diarrhea, stomach pain. Long-term use may lower magnesium.
extra_information: A proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) that lowers stomach acid. Take as prescribed and seek advice if symptoms persist, swallowing becomes difficult, or there is unexplained weight loss. General note: these medicines are for specific digestive symptoms and are not interchangeable. Persistent symptoms, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools need medical assessment.

name: Lansoprazole
uses: Acid reflux, stomach ulcers, H. pylori treatment (with antibiotics).
side_effects: Diarrhea, headache, nausea, stomach pain.
extra_information: A proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) that lowers stomach acid. Often taken before meals; use with antibiotics for H. pylori only as part of the prescribed combination. General note: these medicines are for specific digestive symptoms and are not interchangeable. Persistent symptoms, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools need medical assessment.

name: Famotidine
uses: Acidity, heartburn, stomach ulcers.
side_effects: Headache, dizziness, constipation or diarrhea.
extra_information: An H2 blocker that reduces stomach acid. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney disease; confusion or dizziness can occur, especially in older adults. General note: these medicines are for specific digestive symptoms and are not interchangeable. Persistent symptoms, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools need medical assessment.

name: Domperidone
uses: Nausea, vomiting, bloating, feeling of fullness after meals.
side_effects: Dry mouth, headache, diarrhea. Rarely irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation), especially in high doses or older adults.
extra_information: A medicine for nausea and vomiting in some settings. It can affect heart rhythm and is not suitable for everyone; use only if prescribed and check for interacting medicines. General note: these medicines are for specific digestive symptoms and are not interchangeable. Persistent symptoms, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools need medical assessment.

name: Aluminium Hydroxide + Magnesium Hydroxide + Simethicone
uses: Quick relief from heartburn, acid indigestion and gas.
side_effects: Constipation or diarrhea. May reduce absorption of other medicines taken at the same time.
extra_information: An antacid/anti-gas combination for short-term symptom relief. It can affect absorption of other medicines, so spacing doses may be needed; kidney disease warrants professional advice. General note: these medicines are for specific digestive symptoms and are not interchangeable. Persistent symptoms, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools need medical assessment.

name: Sodium Alginate
uses: Heartburn and acid reflux; forms a protective layer over stomach contents.
side_effects: Bloating, nausea. Contains sodium, so caution in heart or kidney problems.
extra_information: Forms a floating barrier that helps reduce reflux after meals. Follow the product directions; some formulations contain substantial sodium, which may matter with salt restriction. General note: these medicines are for specific digestive symptoms and are not interchangeable. Persistent symptoms, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools need medical assessment.

name: Sucralfate
uses: Stomach and duodenal ulcers; protects the ulcer surface.
side_effects: Constipation, dry mouth. Take apart from other medicines; caution in kidney disease.
extra_information: Coats and protects the ulcer surface rather than directly suppressing acid. It can interfere with absorption of other medicines, so timing should be confirmed with a pharmacist. General note: these medicines are for specific digestive symptoms and are not interchangeable. Persistent symptoms, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools need medical assessment.

name: Ondansetron
uses: Prevents and treats nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy, radiotherapy and surgery.
side_effects: Headache, constipation, diarrhea, dizziness, tiredness. Rarely irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation), serotonin syndrome, allergic reaction.
extra_information: A medicine used to prevent nausea and vomiting. It may cause constipation or headache and can affect heart rhythm in susceptible people; disclose heart problems and other medicines. General note: these medicines are for specific digestive symptoms and are not interchangeable. Persistent symptoms, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools need medical assessment.

name: Paracetamol
uses: Mild to moderate pain (headache, body ache, toothache) and fever.
side_effects: Usually well tolerated. Overdose can seriously damage the liver; rarely rash or nausea.
extra_information: Also called acetaminophen; it relieves pain and fever but not inflammation. Avoid taking multiple products containing paracetamol at once, and seek advice for liver disease or heavy alcohol use. General note: pain relievers differ in their risks and are not interchangeable. Check the active ingredients, avoid duplicate products, and seek advice for severe or persistent pain or fever.

name: Ibuprofen
uses: Pain, inflammation, fever, period pain.
side_effects: Stomach upset, heartburn, ulcers or bleeding; caution with kidney, heart or stomach problems and in pregnancy.
extra_information: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that reduces pain, fever and inflammation. It may irritate the stomach and affect kidneys or blood pressure; avoid combining with other NSAIDs unless advised. General note: pain relievers differ in their risks and are not interchangeable. Check the active ingredients, avoid duplicate products, and seek advice for severe or persistent pain or fever.

name: Ibuprofen + Paracetamol
uses: Headache, body pain, toothache, fever.
side_effects: Stomach upset, heartburn, nausea; same cautions as ibuprofen; avoid taking extra paracetamol.
extra_information: Combines an NSAID with a pain and fever reliever. Check all labels to avoid duplicate ingredients; stomach ulcers, kidney/liver disease, pregnancy, or blood thinners require professional advice. General note: pain relievers differ in their risks and are not interchangeable. Check the active ingredients, avoid duplicate products, and seek advice for severe or persistent pain or fever.

name: Diclofenac
uses: Joint pain, arthritis, muscle pain, post-injury pain.
side_effects: Stomach pain, nausea, ulcers, dizziness. Long-term use raises heart and kidney risks.
extra_information: An NSAID for pain and inflammation. It can increase stomach bleeding and cardiovascular risks and affect kidneys; use the lowest effective amount for the shortest prescribed period. General note: pain relievers differ in their risks and are not interchangeable. Check the active ingredients, avoid duplicate products, and seek advice for severe or persistent pain or fever.

name: Aceclofenac
uses: Pain and inflammation in arthritis, back pain, dental pain.
side_effects: Stomach upset, heartburn, dizziness; caution with ulcers, heart and kidney disease.
extra_information: An NSAID used for inflammatory pain. It may cause stomach irritation, bleeding, kidney problems, or cardiovascular effects; avoid combining with other NSAIDs unless a clinician directs it. General note: pain relievers differ in their risks and are not interchangeable. Check the active ingredients, avoid duplicate products, and seek advice for severe or persistent pain or fever.

name: Naproxen
uses: Arthritis pain, muscle pain, period pain, gout attacks.
side_effects: Stomach upset, heartburn, ulcers or bleeding, fluid retention.
extra_information: An NSAID that can help pain and inflammation. It may cause stomach ulcers/bleeding and kidney or cardiovascular problems; ask a clinician before use with blood thinners or during pregnancy. General note: pain relievers differ in their risks and are not interchangeable. Check the active ingredients, avoid duplicate products, and seek advice for severe or persistent pain or fever.

name: Mefenamic Acid
uses: Period pain, toothache, mild to moderate pain, fever.
side_effects: Stomach upset, diarrhea, drowsiness; avoid with ulcers and kidney problems.
extra_information: An NSAID often used for short-term pain such as period pain. It can cause stomach bleeding and kidney problems; use only as directed and avoid other NSAIDs unless advised. General note: pain relievers differ in their risks and are not interchangeable. Check the active ingredients, avoid duplicate products, and seek advice for severe or persistent pain or fever.

name: Aspirin
uses: Pain, fever; low doses are used to prevent blood clots.
side_effects: Stomach irritation or bleeding. Not for children under 16 (risk of Reye's syndrome).
extra_information: At pain-relieving doses it is an NSAID; low doses may be prescribed to reduce clotting. It increases bleeding risk and is generally avoided in children/teens with viral illness unless specifically directed. General note: pain relievers differ in their risks and are not interchangeable. Check the active ingredients, avoid duplicate products, and seek advice for severe or persistent pain or fever.

name: Etoricoxib
uses: Arthritis, gout and other inflammatory pain (prescription medicine).
side_effects: Stomach upset, high blood pressure, swelling; heart and kidney risks with long use.
extra_information: A COX-2 selective anti-inflammatory prescription medicine. It can raise blood pressure and increase cardiovascular or kidney risks; suitability depends on medical history. General note: pain relievers differ in their risks and are not interchangeable. Check the active ingredients, avoid duplicate products, and seek advice for severe or persistent pain or fever.

name: Tramadol
uses: Moderate to severe pain (prescription medicine only).
side_effects: Drowsiness, dizziness, nausea, constipation; can cause dependence and seizures. Take only as prescribed.
extra_information: An opioid pain medicine that can cause sleepiness, dizziness, constipation, dependence and slowed breathing. Avoid alcohol and driving if impaired; use only exactly as prescribed. General note: pain relievers differ in their risks and are not interchangeable. Check the active ingredients, avoid duplicate products, and seek advice for severe or persistent pain or fever.

name: Sumatriptan
uses: Acute migraine attacks (prescription medicine).
side_effects: Tingling, flushing, chest or throat tightness, drowsiness. Not for people with heart disease.
extra_information: A migraine-specific medicine for an attack, not routine prevention. It is unsuitable for some heart or blood-vessel conditions and can interact with certain antidepressants or other migraine drugs. General note: pain relievers differ in their risks and are not interchangeable. Check the active ingredients, avoid duplicate products, and seek advice for severe or persistent pain or fever.

name: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
uses: Vitamin C deficiency, immune support, helps iron absorption.
side_effects: Stomach upset, diarrhea in high doses; very high doses may contribute to kidney stones.
extra_information: Supports collagen formation and helps the body absorb iron. High supplemental amounts can cause stomach upset and may increase kidney-stone risk in susceptible people. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Vitamin D3 (Cholecalciferol)
uses: Vitamin D deficiency, bone and muscle health, rickets, osteoporosis.
side_effects: Excess causes high blood calcium: nausea, weakness, excessive thirst, kidney problems.
extra_information: Helps the body absorb calcium and maintain bones and muscles. Excessive supplementation can raise blood calcium; follow clinician guidance, especially with kidney disease or calcium supplements. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Vitamin B12 (Methylcobalamin)
uses: Vitamin B12 deficiency, nerve health, some anemias.
side_effects: Mild nausea or diarrhea; rarely rash or itching.
extra_information: Supports red blood cells and nerve function. Deficiency may need testing and a tailored treatment plan; neurological symptoms should be assessed promptly. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Vitamin B-Complex
uses: Prevents or treats B-vitamin deficiency, supports nerves and energy metabolism.
side_effects: Bright yellow urine (harmless), mild nausea. High B6 for long periods can harm nerves.
extra_information: Contains several B vitamins involved in metabolism and nerve function. Formulas vary; avoid taking multiple high-dose supplements without checking the total, especially vitamin B6. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Folic Acid
uses: Anemia from folate deficiency; prevents neural tube defects in pregnancy.
side_effects: Nausea, bloating, loss of appetite. Can mask vitamin B12 deficiency.
extra_information: A form of folate needed for cell growth and red blood cell formation. It is commonly recommended before and early in pregnancy; high doses can mask signs of vitamin B12 deficiency. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Calcium Carbonate
uses: Calcium deficiency, bone strength, osteoporosis.
side_effects: Constipation, gas, bloating; excess may cause kidney stones. Often taken with vitamin D3.
extra_information: Provides calcium and can also act as an antacid. It is generally absorbed best with food and can interfere with thyroid medicine, iron and some antibiotics; confirm dose spacing. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Iron (Ferrous Ascorbate / Ferrous Fumarate)
uses: Iron-deficiency anemia, iron needs in pregnancy.
side_effects: Constipation, dark stools, nausea, stomach pain. Keep away from children; iron overdose is dangerous.
extra_information: Replaces iron stores in iron-deficiency anemia. It can cause constipation, nausea and dark stools; keep iron away from children because overdose can be fatal. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Vitamin E (Tocopherol)
uses: Antioxidant supplement; vitamin E deficiency; used for skin and hair.
side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea; high doses may increase bleeding risk.
extra_information: An antioxidant vitamin; supplementation is mainly useful when intake or levels are inadequate. High doses can increase bleeding risk, especially with anticoagulants. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Zinc
uses: Zinc deficiency, diarrhea in children, immune support, wound healing.
side_effects: Nausea, metallic taste, stomach upset; excess can lower copper levels.
extra_information: Supports immune function and wound healing when zinc is needed. High doses over time can cause copper deficiency and nausea; children's diarrhea treatment should follow local clinical guidance. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Multivitamin + Minerals
uses: Fills nutritional gaps and supports general health.
side_effects: Mild nausea or stomach upset; urine may turn dark yellow.
extra_information: Provides a range of nutrients, but formulations differ and do not replace a balanced diet. Check for duplicate ingredients and ask a clinician before use with pregnancy or regular medicines. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Biotin (Vitamin B7)
uses: Supports hair, skin and nails, mainly when deficiency is present.
side_effects: Rare rash or stomach upset. High doses can interfere with some blood tests (thyroid, heart markers).
extra_information: Biotin deficiency is uncommon; evidence for hair growth is limited when levels are normal. Supplements can interfere with lab tests, including some thyroid and heart tests—tell the lab/clinician. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
uses: Supports heart health; lowers high triglycerides.
side_effects: Fishy burps, loose stools, nausea; high doses may increase bleeding risk.
extra_information: Provides EPA/DHA fatty acids; prescription-strength products may be used for high triglycerides. Supplements can cause fishy aftertaste and may affect bleeding risk at higher doses; check with a clinician. General note: supplements are most useful when a deficiency or increased need exists. More is not always better; high doses can cause harm or interact with medicines.

name: Ofloxacin Ear Drops
uses: Bacterial infections of the outer ear and the middle ear.
side_effects: Local irritation, itching, ear pain, temporary taste change.
extra_information: An antibiotic ear preparation for susceptible bacterial infections. Use only in the affected ear as prescribed; keep the tip clean and seek review for worsening pain, fever or hearing changes. General note: ear drops are formulation-specific and must be used only in the ear. Ear pain with fever, discharge, sudden hearing loss, or a possible eardrum injury needs medical assessment.

name: Ciprofloxacin + Dexamethasone Ear Drops
uses: Bacterial ear infection with swelling or inflammation.
side_effects: Ear itching, irritation, burning. Do not use for long without medical advice.
extra_information: Combines an antibiotic with a steroid to treat infection and inflammation. Use for the prescribed duration and route only; seek review if symptoms worsen or do not improve. General note: ear drops are formulation-specific and must be used only in the ear. Ear pain with fever, discharge, sudden hearing loss, or a possible eardrum injury needs medical assessment.

name: Clotrimazole Ear Drops
uses: Fungal infections of the outer ear canal.
side_effects: Local burning, redness or irritation.
extra_information: An antifungal preparation for certain fungal ear infections. Use only as directed and do not put it in the eye; persistent pain or discharge needs medical review. General note: ear drops are formulation-specific and must be used only in the ear. Ear pain with fever, discharge, sudden hearing loss, or a possible eardrum injury needs medical assessment.

name: Docusate Sodium Ear Drops
uses: Softens hardened ear wax so it can be removed.
side_effects: Mild irritation or redness. Not to be used if the eardrum is perforated.
extra_information: Softens hardened earwax to help removal. Do not use without medical advice if there is ear discharge, a perforated eardrum, ear tubes, prior ear surgery or significant pain. General note: ear drops are formulation-specific and must be used only in the ear. Ear pain with fever, discharge, sudden hearing loss, or a possible eardrum injury needs medical assessment.

name: Carbamide Peroxide Ear Drops
uses: Softens and loosens ear wax.
side_effects: Temporary fizzing, mild irritation or discomfort.
extra_information: Helps soften earwax for easier removal. Avoid use with a perforated eardrum, ear tubes, infection or unexplained ear pain unless a clinician advises it. General note: ear drops are formulation-specific and must be used only in the ear. Ear pain with fever, discharge, sudden hearing loss, or a possible eardrum injury needs medical assessment.

name: Moxifloxacin Eye Drops
uses: Bacterial conjunctivitis (eye infection).
side_effects: Stinging, eye irritation, temporary blurred vision.
extra_information: An antibiotic for certain bacterial eye infections; it does not treat viral or allergic conjunctivitis. Wash hands, avoid touching the bottle tip, and seek care for eye pain or vision changes. General note: eye drops must be used only as directed, with clean hands and no contact between the bottle tip and the eye. Eye pain, light sensitivity or vision changes require prompt assessment.

name: Ciprofloxacin Eye Drops
uses: Bacterial eye infections.
side_effects: Stinging, redness, white deposit on cornea (rare), bitter taste.
extra_information: An antibiotic eye preparation for susceptible bacterial infections. Finish the prescribed course; contact a clinician if pain, light sensitivity or vision problems occur. General note: eye drops must be used only as directed, with clean hands and no contact between the bottle tip and the eye. Eye pain, light sensitivity or vision changes require prompt assessment.

name: Tobramycin Eye Drops
uses: Bacterial eye infections.
side_effects: Eye irritation, redness, itching, swelling of the eyelids.
extra_information: An antibiotic for certain bacterial eye infections. Use only in the eye and as prescribed; prolonged use can encourage resistant organisms or fungal overgrowth. General note: eye drops must be used only as directed, with clean hands and no contact between the bottle tip and the eye. Eye pain, light sensitivity or vision changes require prompt assessment.

name: Tobramycin + Dexamethasone Eye Drops
uses: Eye infections with inflammation, or after eye surgery.
side_effects: Raised eye pressure, delayed healing with long use; eye irritation.
extra_information: Combines an antibiotic with a steroid. Eye steroids can raise eye pressure or worsen some infections, so use only under eye-care supervision and for the prescribed duration. General note: eye drops must be used only as directed, with clean hands and no contact between the bottle tip and the eye. Eye pain, light sensitivity or vision changes require prompt assessment.

name: Carboxymethylcellulose Eye Drops
uses: Dry eyes; lubricating artificial tears.
side_effects: Temporary blurred vision, mild stinging.
extra_information: Lubricating artificial tears for dry-eye symptoms. Preservative-free products may be preferable for frequent use; remove contact lenses if the label instructs you to. General note: eye drops must be used only as directed, with clean hands and no contact between the bottle tip and the eye. Eye pain, light sensitivity or vision changes require prompt assessment.

name: Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose Eye Drops
uses: Dry, tired or irritated eyes.
side_effects: Temporary blurred vision, mild irritation.
extra_information: Lubricates the eye to ease dryness and irritation. Temporary blurred vision can occur after use; avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye. General note: eye drops must be used only as directed, with clean hands and no contact between the bottle tip and the eye. Eye pain, light sensitivity or vision changes require prompt assessment.

name: Olopatadine Eye Drops
uses: Allergic conjunctivitis: itchy, watery, red eyes.
side_effects: Stinging, headache, dry eye, taste disturbance.
extra_information: An antihistamine/mast-cell stabilizer for allergic eye symptoms. It does not treat bacterial infection; avoid touching the bottle tip and follow contact-lens instructions on the label. General note: eye drops must be used only as directed, with clean hands and no contact between the bottle tip and the eye. Eye pain, light sensitivity or vision changes require prompt assessment.

name: Timolol Eye Drops
uses: Glaucoma and high eye pressure.
side_effects: Slow heartbeat, breathing difficulty in asthma, tiredness. Needs medical supervision.
extra_information: Lowers eye pressure in glaucoma. Some medicine can enter the bloodstream and affect heart rate or breathing; tell the prescriber about asthma, slow pulse or heart disease. General note: eye drops must be used only as directed, with clean hands and no contact between the bottle tip and the eye. Eye pain, light sensitivity or vision changes require prompt assessment.

name: Latanoprost Eye Drops
uses: Glaucoma and high eye pressure.
side_effects: Red eyes, darkening of the iris or eyelid skin, longer eyelashes.
extra_information: Lowers eye pressure in glaucoma and is usually used regularly. It may gradually darken iris or eyelid pigmentation and change eyelash growth; do not stop without eye-care advice. General note: eye drops must be used only as directed, with clean hands and no contact between the bottle tip and the eye. Eye pain, light sensitivity or vision changes require prompt assessment.

name: Prednisolone Eye Drops
uses: Eye inflammation (steroid, prescription medicine).
side_effects: Raised eye pressure, cataract and infections with prolonged use.
extra_information: A corticosteroid for selected inflammatory eye conditions. It can raise eye pressure and worsen infections, so it requires clinician supervision and follow-up. General note: eye drops must be used only as directed, with clean hands and no contact between the bottle tip and the eye. Eye pain, light sensitivity or vision changes require prompt assessment.

name: Minoxidil (Topical)
uses: Hair loss from androgenetic alopecia (pattern baldness).
side_effects: Scalp itching or dryness, unwanted facial hair; rarely dizziness or fast heartbeat.
extra_information: Used consistently over months for pattern hair loss; benefit usually needs ongoing use and may reverse after stopping. Apply to the scalp as directed and seek advice for chest pain, rapid heartbeat or swelling. General note: hair treatments often need consistent use for several months and may not work for every cause of hair loss. Sudden, patchy or scarring hair loss should be evaluated.

name: Finasteride 1 mg
uses: Male pattern hair loss (prescription medicine, men only).
side_effects: Reduced sex drive, erectile problems, breast tenderness. Women who are or may be pregnant must not handle crushed tablets.
extra_information: Prescription treatment for male pattern hair loss; results take months and may fade after stopping. Possible sexual or mood-related adverse effects should be discussed with the prescriber; it must not be handled by pregnant people if crushed/broken. General note: hair treatments often need consistent use for several months and may not work for every cause of hair loss. Sudden, patchy or scarring hair loss should be evaluated.

name: Ketoconazole Shampoo
uses: Dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, scalp fungal infection.
side_effects: Scalp irritation, oily or dry hair, rarely hair texture change.
extra_information: Antifungal shampoo for dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis. Leave on for the label-recommended time before rinsing; stop and seek advice if severe irritation develops. General note: hair treatments often need consistent use for several months and may not work for every cause of hair loss. Sudden, patchy or scarring hair loss should be evaluated.

name: Clotrimazole Cream
uses: Fungal skin infections: ringworm, athlete's foot, jock itch, candidiasis.
side_effects: Local burning, redness, itching.
extra_information: An antifungal for skin infections; improvement may take days and treatment often needs to continue as directed. Keep the area dry and avoid using it in the eyes or mouth. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Terbinafine
uses: Fungal infections of skin and nails (cream or tablets).
side_effects: Cream: local irritation. Tablets: headache, stomach upset, taste change; rarely liver problems.
extra_information: An antifungal available as topical products and tablets. Oral treatment can affect the liver and interact with medicines; seek medical advice for jaundice, dark urine or persistent nausea. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Luliconazole Cream
uses: Ringworm, athlete's foot and jock itch.
side_effects: Local burning, redness, itching.
extra_information: A topical antifungal for selected fungal skin infections. Apply to clean, dry skin as prescribed and avoid eyes, mouth and internal use unless the product is specifically intended for it. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Ketoconazole Cream
uses: Fungal skin infections, tinea versicolor, seborrheic dermatitis.
side_effects: Local irritation, itching, burning.
extra_information: An antifungal for certain skin fungal conditions. Use on the affected skin as directed; it is not the same as oral ketoconazole, which has important safety risks. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Mupirocin Ointment
uses: Bacterial skin infections such as impetigo and infected cuts.
side_effects: Burning, stinging, itching at the site.
extra_information: A topical antibiotic for selected bacterial skin infections. Use only on the specified area for the prescribed course; repeated or prolonged use can promote resistance. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Fusidic Acid Cream
uses: Bacterial skin infections such as boils and infected wounds.
side_effects: Local itching, redness, rash.
extra_information: A topical antibiotic for certain bacterial skin infections. Use only when indicated and for the prescribed duration to reduce antibiotic resistance. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Silver Sulfadiazine Cream
uses: Prevents and treats infection in burns.
side_effects: Skin irritation, burning; avoid in sulfa allergy.
extra_information: Used for selected burn wounds under medical guidance. It is not suitable for everyone, including some people with sulfonamide allergy; burn care should be assessed by a professional. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Povidone-Iodine
uses: Antiseptic for cuts, wounds and before minor procedures.
side_effects: Skin irritation; avoid in iodine allergy; excess use on large wounds may affect thyroid.
extra_information: An antiseptic that reduces germs on skin. Formulations differ, so use only on the intended area; repeated extensive use may affect thyroid function and requires caution in pregnancy or thyroid disease. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Hydrocortisone Cream
uses: Mild eczema, itching, insect bites, dermatitis.
side_effects: Skin thinning or irritation with prolonged use; avoid on infected skin.
extra_information: A mild topical steroid for short-term relief of inflammation and itching. Use a thin layer as directed; avoid prolonged use on the face, groin or broken skin unless advised. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Betamethasone Cream
uses: Eczema, psoriasis, allergic skin rashes.
side_effects: Skin thinning, stretch marks, irritation; use short term only.
extra_information: A topical corticosteroid for inflammatory skin conditions. Strength varies by formulation; prolonged or extensive use can thin skin, so follow the prescribed amount and duration. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Clobetasol Cream
uses: Severe eczema, psoriasis and other inflammatory skin conditions (strong steroid).
side_effects: Skin thinning, stretch marks, acne; do not use on face or for long periods unless prescribed.
extra_information: A very potent topical steroid for selected severe skin conditions. Use only as prescribed, usually for a limited period; avoid face/groin use unless specifically directed. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Calamine Lotion
uses: Soothes itching from rashes, chickenpox, insect bites and heat rash.
side_effects: Skin dryness or irritation in some people.
extra_information: Soothes itchy, irritated skin but does not treat the underlying cause of every rash. For external use only; avoid eyes and seek advice for severe, spreading or infected rashes. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Permethrin Cream
uses: Treats scabies and head lice.
side_effects: Temporary itching, burning, redness at the application site.
extra_information: Used to treat scabies; household contacts and bedding/clothing may also need coordinated treatment. Follow the exact application and repeat-treatment instructions provided by a clinician or product label. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Adapalene Gel
uses: Acne (blackheads, whiteheads, pimples).
side_effects: Dryness, redness, peeling, sun sensitivity. Use sunscreen.
extra_information: A topical retinoid for acne; dryness and irritation are common early on, and improvement may take several weeks. Use sun protection and ask a clinician before use during pregnancy. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Benzoyl Peroxide Gel
uses: Mild to moderate acne.
side_effects: Dryness, peeling, redness, may bleach clothes and hair.
extra_information: Helps acne by reducing acne-causing bacteria and blocked pores. It can irritate skin and bleach fabrics; start as directed and use moisturizer/sun protection if needed. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Clindamycin Gel
uses: Acne caused by bacteria.
side_effects: Dryness, redness, itching; rarely diarrhea.
extra_information: A topical antibiotic for acne, often combined with benzoyl peroxide to reduce resistance. Use as prescribed; prolonged antibiotic-only treatment is generally avoided. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Tretinoin Cream
uses: Acne and skin renewal (prescription medicine).
side_effects: Redness, peeling, dryness, sun sensitivity; avoid in pregnancy.
extra_information: A topical retinoid for acne and skin renewal; irritation and sun sensitivity can occur. Use as prescribed, avoid excessive application, and do not use during pregnancy unless a specialist explicitly advises otherwise. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Isotretinoin
uses: Severe acne (prescription medicine, strict medical supervision).
side_effects: Very dry lips and skin, mood changes, high lipids; causes serious birth defects, so pregnancy must be avoided.
extra_information: An oral retinoid reserved for severe acne under specialist supervision. It can cause serious birth defects and requires strict pregnancy prevention/monitoring where relevant, plus monitoring for adverse effects. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Salicylic Acid
uses: Acne, warts, corns, dandruff and rough skin.
side_effects: Local irritation, dryness, peeling.
extra_information: Helps loosen dead skin and unclog pores; concentration and formulation determine appropriate use. Avoid applying to large areas or damaged skin without advice, especially in children. General note: skin products differ greatly in strength and purpose. Avoid combining active products without guidance and seek assessment for rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, pus or fever.

name: Paracetamol + Phenylephrine + Chlorpheniramine
uses: Relieves cold and flu symptoms: blocked nose, sneezing, runny nose, mild fever and body ache.
side_effects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, nervousness, fast heartbeat. Caution in high blood pressure, heart disease and glaucoma.
extra_information: Combination cold medicine for symptom relief, not a cure for the infection. It may cause drowsiness and raise blood pressure; avoid duplicate paracetamol and check suitability with a pharmacist. General note: combination cold products can contain overlapping ingredients. Check labels carefully and ask a pharmacist about use in children, pregnancy, high blood pressure or chronic illness.

name: Cetirizine + Paracetamol + Phenylephrine
uses: Cold with allergy symptoms: sneezing, runny nose, congestion, fever, headache.
side_effects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, restlessness, increased blood pressure or heart rate.
extra_information: Combination product for allergy/cold symptoms. Check for duplicate paracetamol, drowsiness and blood-pressure effects; ask a pharmacist if you have hypertension, glaucoma or other conditions. General note: combination cold products can contain overlapping ingredients. Check labels carefully and ask a pharmacist about use in children, pregnancy, high blood pressure or chronic illness.

name: Paracetamol + Phenylephrine + Caffeine
uses: Relieves cold and flu symptoms: blocked nose, headache, fever and body ache.
side_effects: Nervousness, sleeplessness, fast heartbeat; caution in high blood pressure and heart disease.
extra_information: Combination symptom reliever. Caffeine may cause jitters or insomnia and phenylephrine may raise blood pressure; avoid duplicate paracetamol-containing products. General note: combination cold products can contain overlapping ingredients. Check labels carefully and ask a pharmacist about use in children, pregnancy, high blood pressure or chronic illness.

name: Pseudoephedrine
uses: Relieves nasal and sinus congestion.
side_effects: Restlessness, sleeplessness, fast heartbeat, raised blood pressure. Caution in heart disease and prostate problems.
extra_information: A decongestant that can cause insomnia, palpitations and raised blood pressure. Check with a pharmacist first if you have hypertension, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease or take stimulant/MAOI medicines. General note: combination cold products can contain overlapping ingredients. Check labels carefully and ask a pharmacist about use in children, pregnancy, high blood pressure or chronic illness.

name: Xylometazoline Nasal Drops
uses: Quick relief from a blocked nose due to cold, sinusitis or allergy.
side_effects: Nasal dryness, burning, sneezing. Using it for more than a few days can cause rebound congestion.
extra_information: A fast-acting nasal decongestant for short-term use only. Using it too many days in a row can cause rebound congestion; follow the package duration limit. General note: combination cold products can contain overlapping ingredients. Check labels carefully and ask a pharmacist about use in children, pregnancy, high blood pressure or chronic illness.

name: Oxymetazoline Nasal Drops
uses: Short-term relief of blocked nose.
side_effects: Nasal irritation, dryness. Prolonged use causes rebound congestion.
extra_information: Provides short-term relief of nasal blockage. Overuse can cause rebound congestion; use only for the label-recommended number of days. General note: combination cold products can contain overlapping ingredients. Check labels carefully and ask a pharmacist about use in children, pregnancy, high blood pressure or chronic illness.

name: Saline Nasal Drops (Sodium Chloride)
uses: Loosens mucus and clears a blocked nose; safe for regular use.
side_effects: Mild nasal irritation or sneezing.
extra_information: Moistens nasal passages and loosens mucus without a decongestant drug. Use clean equipment and follow hygiene directions, especially for infants. General note: combination cold products can contain overlapping ingredients. Check labels carefully and ask a pharmacist about use in children, pregnancy, high blood pressure or chronic illness.

name: Levocetirizine + Montelukast
uses: Allergic rhinitis: sneezing, runny and blocked nose, itching (prescription medicine).
side_effects: Drowsiness, headache, dry mouth. Montelukast can rarely cause mood or sleep changes.
extra_information: Combines an antihistamine with a leukotriene blocker for selected allergy symptoms. Montelukast has a warning for serious mood or behavior changes; seek medical advice if these occur. General note: combination cold products can contain overlapping ingredients. Check labels carefully and ask a pharmacist about use in children, pregnancy, high blood pressure or chronic illness.

name: Menthol + Camphor Balm
uses: External relief from nasal congestion and cold symptoms.
side_effects: Skin irritation. Not for use inside the nose or on broken skin, and not for babies under 2 years.
extra_information: Provides a cooling/warming sensation that may temporarily ease congestion discomfort. External use only; do not swallow, place in nostrils, or apply to broken skin, and keep away from children. General note: combination cold products can contain overlapping ingredients. Check labels carefully and ask a pharmacist about use in children, pregnancy, high blood pressure or chronic illness.

name: Dextromethorphan
uses: Relieves dry, irritating cough.
side_effects: Drowsiness, dizziness, nausea. Can cause serious reactions with some antidepressants; avoid alcohol.
extra_information: A cough suppressant for selected dry coughs. It can interact dangerously with MAO inhibitors and some antidepressants; check combination products and avoid use for persistent or unexplained cough without advice. General note: cough medicines target different symptoms and are not suitable for every cough. Seek urgent care for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips or coughing blood; get medical advice for a persistent cough.

name: Diphenhydramine + Ammonium Chloride + Sodium Citrate
uses: Relieves cough with throat irritation and allergic symptoms.
side_effects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, dizziness; caution in glaucoma, prostate problems and for children.
extra_information: Combination cough medicine that may cause drowsiness, dry mouth or stomach upset. Avoid alcohol and driving if sleepy; check suitability for children and people with chronic conditions. General note: cough medicines target different symptoms and are not suitable for every cough. Seek urgent care for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips or coughing blood; get medical advice for a persistent cough.

name: Ambroxol
uses: Loosens thick mucus and makes a wet (productive) cough easier to clear.
side_effects: Nausea, stomach upset, mild diarrhea; rarely allergic rash.
extra_information: A mucolytic that helps loosen thick mucus in a productive cough. Stop and seek advice if rash, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs; persistent cough needs assessment. General note: cough medicines target different symptoms and are not suitable for every cough. Seek urgent care for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips or coughing blood; get medical advice for a persistent cough.

name: Bromhexine
uses: Thins and loosens mucus in chest congestion and wet cough.
side_effects: Nausea, stomach upset, rash; caution in stomach ulcers.
extra_information: Helps thin mucus so it is easier to clear. Use as directed and seek advice for a persistent cough, blood in sputum or breathing difficulty. General note: cough medicines target different symptoms and are not suitable for every cough. Seek urgent care for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips or coughing blood; get medical advice for a persistent cough.

name: Guaifenesin
uses: Expectorant: loosens phlegm and makes coughing up mucus easier.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, stomach upset.
extra_information: An expectorant that helps loosen mucus; drinking fluids may also help. Follow the label and seek medical advice if cough lasts, worsens or is accompanied by fever or shortness of breath. General note: cough medicines target different symptoms and are not suitable for every cough. Seek urgent care for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips or coughing blood; get medical advice for a persistent cough.

name: Levosalbutamol + Ambroxol + Guaifenesin
uses: Wet cough with wheezing or chest tightness.
side_effects: Tremor, fast heartbeat, nervousness, headache. Caution in heart disease and high blood pressure.
extra_information: Combines a bronchodilator with mucus-loosening ingredients. It may cause tremor, palpitations or restlessness; wheezing or breathlessness that is severe or worsening needs urgent assessment. General note: cough medicines target different symptoms and are not suitable for every cough. Seek urgent care for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips or coughing blood; get medical advice for a persistent cough.

name: Acetylcysteine
uses: Loosens thick mucus in chest conditions.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, unpleasant smell or taste.
extra_information: A mucolytic that breaks down thick mucus; it is also used in a different medical setting for paracetamol overdose. Formulations and uses differ, so use only as directed and seek advice for wheezing or allergic reactions. General note: cough medicines target different symptoms and are not suitable for every cough. Seek urgent care for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips or coughing blood; get medical advice for a persistent cough.

name: Salbutamol
uses: Wheezing, shortness of breath and cough due to asthma or COPD (relief inhaler or tablets).
side_effects: Tremor, fast heartbeat, headache, nervousness.
extra_information: A quick-relief bronchodilator for asthma-related wheezing. Frequent need for it can signal poor asthma control; seek urgent care if breathing difficulty is severe or relief is not lasting. General note: cough medicines target different symptoms and are not suitable for every cough. Seek urgent care for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips or coughing blood; get medical advice for a persistent cough.

name: Montelukast
uses: Prevents asthma attacks and allergic rhinitis (prescription medicine).
side_effects: Headache, stomach pain; rarely mood changes, sleep problems or agitation.
extra_information: Used for asthma control or allergic rhinitis, not for immediate relief of an asthma attack. It carries a warning for possible serious mood or behavior changes; discuss risks and alternatives with the prescriber. General note: cough medicines target different symptoms and are not suitable for every cough. Seek urgent care for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips or coughing blood; get medical advice for a persistent cough.

name: Honey + Herbal Cough Syrup (Tulsi, Mulethi)
uses: Soothes throat irritation and mild cough.
side_effects: Generally mild; may upset the stomach. Honey should not be given to infants under 1 year.
extra_information: May soothe throat irritation, but evidence and ingredients vary by product. Do not give honey to children under 1 year; licorice (mulethi) can affect blood pressure and potassium. General note: cough medicines target different symptoms and are not suitable for every cough. Seek urgent care for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips or coughing blood; get medical advice for a persistent cough.

name: Throat Lozenges (Amylmetacresol / Menthol)
uses: Soothes sore throat and mild cough.
side_effects: Mild mouth irritation or stomach upset; not for young children.
extra_information: Provide temporary relief of sore-throat discomfort. Follow age and label directions, avoid choking risk in young children, and seek care for difficulty breathing/swallowing or persistent high fever. General note: cough medicines target different symptoms and are not suitable for every cough. Seek urgent care for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips or coughing blood; get medical advice for a persistent cough.

name: Hydroxyzine
uses: Relieves severe itching from allergies, hives and skin conditions; also used for anxiety (prescription medicine).
side_effects: Marked drowsiness, dry mouth, dizziness. Avoid driving and alcohol.
extra_information: A sedating antihistamine that can cause drowsiness and affect heart rhythm in some people. Avoid alcohol and driving if affected; tell the prescriber about heart conditions and other sedating medicines. General note: anti-itch products may treat symptoms or the underlying cause, depending on the ingredient. Avoid prolonged steroid use without guidance and seek assessment for widespread rash, swelling or breathing problems.

name: Bilastine
uses: Allergic rhinitis and hives: itching, sneezing, watery eyes.
side_effects: Headache, drowsiness, dizziness; take on an empty stomach.
extra_information: A relatively non-sedating antihistamine for allergy symptoms and hives. Food and fruit juice can reduce absorption, so follow the product's timing instructions. General note: anti-itch products may treat symptoms or the underlying cause, depending on the ingredient. Avoid prolonged steroid use without guidance and seek assessment for widespread rash, swelling or breathing problems.

name: Desloratadine
uses: Allergic rhinitis and chronic hives with itching.
side_effects: Headache, dry mouth, tiredness.
extra_information: An antihistamine for allergic rhinitis and hives, usually less sedating than older antihistamines. Follow dosing instructions and seek advice if symptoms persist or side effects occur. General note: anti-itch products may treat symptoms or the underlying cause, depending on the ingredient. Avoid prolonged steroid use without guidance and seek assessment for widespread rash, swelling or breathing problems.

name: Crotamiton
uses: Relieves itching and helps treat scabies.
side_effects: Local skin irritation, redness; avoid on broken skin or near eyes.
extra_information: A topical medicine used for itching and, in some formulations, scabies. Follow the product-specific instructions; avoid eyes and mucous membranes and get medical advice if symptoms persist. General note: anti-itch products may treat symptoms or the underlying cause, depending on the ingredient. Avoid prolonged steroid use without guidance and seek assessment for widespread rash, swelling or breathing problems.

name: Mometasone Cream
uses: Itchy and inflamed skin: eczema, dermatitis, psoriasis.
side_effects: Skin thinning, stretch marks, burning with prolonged use; avoid on the face for long periods.
extra_information: A topical steroid for inflammatory skin conditions. Use a thin layer for the prescribed duration; prolonged use or use on sensitive areas can cause skin thinning. General note: anti-itch products may treat symptoms or the underlying cause, depending on the ingredient. Avoid prolonged steroid use without guidance and seek assessment for widespread rash, swelling or breathing problems.

name: Tacrolimus Ointment
uses: Eczema (atopic dermatitis) and chronic itchy skin conditions (prescription medicine).
side_effects: Burning or itching at the site, sun sensitivity; avoid extra sun exposure.
extra_information: A non-steroid topical immune-modulating treatment for eczema. Temporary burning can occur; avoid unapproved use and discuss infection, sun exposure and long-term plans with the prescriber. General note: anti-itch products may treat symptoms or the underlying cause, depending on the ingredient. Avoid prolonged steroid use without guidance and seek assessment for widespread rash, swelling or breathing problems.

name: Menthol + Zinc Oxide Lotion
uses: Soothes itching and heat rash.
side_effects: Skin irritation in sensitive skin; avoid broken skin.
extra_information: Can soothe itching and protect irritated skin, but does not treat every cause of rash. External use only; stop if irritation worsens and seek advice for spreading or infected skin. General note: anti-itch products may treat symptoms or the underlying cause, depending on the ingredient. Avoid prolonged steroid use without guidance and seek assessment for widespread rash, swelling or breathing problems.

name: Cetirizine
uses: Relieves allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose and itching.
side_effects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, headache.
extra_information: An antihistamine for sneezing, itching and hives; some people still feel sleepy. Avoid alcohol if it increases drowsiness and check dose suitability in kidney disease. General note: antihistamines can cause drowsiness and interact with alcohol or sedating medicines. Seek urgent help for throat/tongue swelling or difficulty breathing.

name: Levocetirizine
uses: Allergic rhinitis, hives and itching.
side_effects: Drowsiness, tiredness, dry mouth.
extra_information: An antihistamine for allergic rhinitis and hives. It can cause sleepiness and may need dose adjustment with kidney impairment; avoid alcohol if drowsy. General note: antihistamines can cause drowsiness and interact with alcohol or sedating medicines. Seek urgent help for throat/tongue swelling or difficulty breathing.

name: Fexofenadine
uses: Hay fever and chronic hives.
side_effects: Headache, dizziness, nausea; usually less sleepy than older antihistamines.
extra_information: An antihistamine that is usually less sedating. Fruit juices and aluminium/magnesium antacids can reduce absorption, so follow label instructions about timing. General note: antihistamines can cause drowsiness and interact with alcohol or sedating medicines. Seek urgent help for throat/tongue swelling or difficulty breathing.

name: Loratadine
uses: Allergic rhinitis and skin allergies.
side_effects: Headache, dry mouth, mild drowsiness.
extra_information: An antihistamine for allergy symptoms and hives, generally less sedating than older options. Follow the label and ask a clinician about dose suitability in significant liver disease. General note: antihistamines can cause drowsiness and interact with alcohol or sedating medicines. Seek urgent help for throat/tongue swelling or difficulty breathing.

name: Chlorpheniramine
uses: Cold and allergy symptoms: sneezing, runny nose, itching.
side_effects: Marked drowsiness, dry mouth, blurred vision, urinary difficulty.
extra_information: An older, sedating antihistamine that may cause drowsiness, dry mouth and blurred vision. Avoid alcohol and driving if affected; use caution in older adults and with glaucoma or urinary retention. General note: antihistamines can cause drowsiness and interact with alcohol or sedating medicines. Seek urgent help for throat/tongue swelling or difficulty breathing.

name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS)
uses: Prevention and treatment of dehydration from diarrhea or vomiting.
side_effects: Usually well tolerated when mixed correctly; incorrect concentration can cause electrolyte problems.
extra_information: Replaces water and salts lost through diarrhea or vomiting; mix the sachet with exactly the amount of safe water stated on the packet and discard leftovers as directed. Seek urgent care for severe dehydration, confusion, very little urine, blood in stool, or inability to keep fluids down.

name: Zinc Sulfate
uses: Zinc supplementation; sometimes used with ORS for childhood diarrhea under local clinical guidance.
side_effects: Nausea, stomach upset, metallic taste; excess intake can cause copper deficiency.
extra_information: Use for a defined indication and follow age-appropriate product instructions. It can reduce absorption of some antibiotics, so a pharmacist may advise separating doses. Avoid prolonged high-dose supplementation unless medically supervised.

name: Amoxicillin
uses: Certain bacterial infections when prescribed, such as some ear, throat, chest, dental or urinary infections.
side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, rash; rare but serious allergic reaction.
extra_information: Prescription antibiotic; it does not treat viral colds or flu. Take only for the infection and duration prescribed, disclose penicillin allergy, and seek emergency help for facial swelling or breathing difficulty. Severe or bloody diarrhea needs medical review.

name: Azithromycin
uses: Selected bacterial respiratory, skin and other infections when prescribed.
side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain; rarely heart-rhythm problems or liver injury.
extra_information: An antibiotic that is not appropriate for every cough, sore throat or fever. It can interact with other medicines and may affect heart rhythm; use only after a clinician assesses the likely infection and your medical history.

name: Cefixime
uses: Certain bacterial infections when prescribed.
side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, abdominal discomfort, rash.
extra_information: A cephalosporin antibiotic; it will not help viral infections. Tell the prescriber about serious penicillin or cephalosporin allergies and kidney disease. Do not share leftover antibiotics or self-start treatment.

name: Metronidazole
uses: Selected anaerobic bacterial and protozoal infections when prescribed.
side_effects: Nausea, metallic taste, abdominal discomfort, headache.
extra_information: Used for specific infections, not as a general stomach medicine. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for the period stated in the product/clinician advice after the last dose; check interactions, especially with warfarin, and seek advice for numbness or severe rash.

name: Albendazole
uses: Treatment of certain intestinal worm infections.
side_effects: Abdominal pain, nausea, headache; longer courses may affect liver tests or blood counts.
extra_information: The appropriate regimen depends on the parasite, age and clinical situation; do not assume one dose treats every worm infection. Pregnancy, liver disease, and repeated or prolonged courses require clinician guidance.

name: Loperamide
uses: Short-term symptom relief for some cases of acute diarrhea in adults.
side_effects: Constipation, cramps, nausea; excessive doses can cause dangerous heart-rhythm problems.
extra_information: It treats symptoms, not the cause, and does not replace oral rehydration. Avoid self-use with bloody stools, high fever, severe abdominal pain, or suspected invasive infection; do not give to young children unless a clinician directs it.

name: Lactulose
uses: Constipation; also used under medical supervision for hepatic encephalopathy.
side_effects: Gas, bloating, abdominal cramps, diarrhea.
extra_information: An osmotic laxative that draws water into the bowel and may take a day or two to work. Maintain suitable fluid intake; prolonged diarrhea can disturb electrolytes. Seek assessment for severe pain, vomiting, or suspected bowel obstruction.

name: Polyethylene Glycol (Macrogol)
uses: Constipation; some formulations are used for bowel preparation under medical direction.
side_effects: Bloating, nausea, cramps, loose stools.
extra_information: An osmotic laxative that softens stool by retaining water in the bowel. Follow the specific product instructions because formulations differ. Seek medical advice for persistent constipation, rectal bleeding, severe pain, or vomiting.

name: Metformin
uses: Type 2 diabetes, alongside lifestyle measures; sometimes other clinician-directed indications.
side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, abdominal discomfort; long-term use may lower vitamin B12.
extra_information: Helps lower blood glucose and is often taken with food to reduce stomach upset. Kidney function should be checked; serious illness, dehydration, or certain contrast scans may require clinician advice about temporarily holding it. Do not change treatment without guidance.

name: Glimepiride
uses: Type 2 diabetes when prescribed.
side_effects: Low blood sugar, dizziness, nausea, weight gain.
extra_information: Stimulates insulin release and can cause hypoglycemia, especially when meals are delayed or skipped. Learn the signs of low blood sugar and discuss what to do with your care team; extra caution is needed with kidney or liver impairment.

name: Amlodipine
uses: High blood pressure and some forms of angina.
side_effects: Ankle swelling, flushing, headache, dizziness.
extra_information: A calcium-channel blocker that relaxes blood vessels. Take consistently as prescribed and do not stop or adjust it on your own. Report troublesome swelling, fainting, or worsening chest pain; it is not a treatment for sudden chest-pain emergencies.

name: Telmisartan
uses: High blood pressure; selected cardiovascular or kidney-risk situations under clinician guidance.
side_effects: Dizziness, low blood pressure; may raise potassium or affect kidney function.
extra_information: An angiotensin-receptor blocker. Blood pressure, kidney function and potassium may need monitoring. It must not be used during pregnancy; check with a clinician before using potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes.

name: Atorvastatin
uses: High cholesterol and reduction of cardiovascular risk.
side_effects: Muscle aches, digestive symptoms; rarely serious muscle or liver problems.
extra_information: A statin that lowers LDL cholesterol and helps reduce heart attack and stroke risk over time. Report unexplained severe muscle pain or weakness, especially with dark urine. Discuss pregnancy, liver disease and interacting medicines with the prescriber.

name: Levothyroxine
uses: Thyroid hormone replacement for hypothyroidism.
side_effects: Excess dosing may cause palpitations, tremor, sweating, anxiety or insomnia.
extra_information: Usually taken consistently on an empty stomach as directed. Iron, calcium and some antacids can reduce absorption, so doses often need to be separated by several hours according to professional advice. Thyroid blood tests guide dose changes; do not adjust based on symptoms alone.

name: Ferrous Sulfate
uses: Iron replacement for iron deficiency when indicated.
side_effects: Constipation, nausea, abdominal discomfort, dark stools.
extra_information: Iron is best used when deficiency is suspected or confirmed and the cause is assessed. Keep iron products away from children because overdose can be fatal. It interacts with levothyroxine and some antibiotics; ask a pharmacist about dose spacing.

name: Calcium + Vitamin D3
uses: Supplementation when dietary intake or vitamin D/calcium levels are inadequate.
side_effects: Constipation, bloating; excessive intake may cause high calcium or kidney stones.
extra_information: Need depends on diet, age, health conditions and lab results. Calcium can interfere with absorption of levothyroxine, iron and some antibiotics, so timing may need separation. Kidney disease or a history of stones warrants professional advice.

name: Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3)
uses: Prevention or treatment of vitamin D deficiency.
side_effects: Usually none at recommended amounts; excessive doses can cause high calcium, nausea, weakness or kidney problems.
extra_information: Vitamin D supports calcium absorption and bone health. High-dose weekly or monthly products should be used only according to the prescribed schedule; taking too much can be harmful. Do not combine multiple high-dose vitamin D products without advice.

name: Budesonide Inhaler
uses: Controller treatment to reduce airway inflammation in asthma and selected respiratory conditions.
side_effects: Hoarse voice, throat irritation, oral thrush.
extra_information: An inhaled corticosteroid used regularly for control, not for immediate relief of a sudden asthma attack unless the specific prescribed plan says otherwise. Rinse and spit after use; correct inhaler technique matters. Do not stop a controller abruptly without medical advice.

name: Artificial Tears (Lubricating Eye Drops)
uses: Temporary relief of dry, gritty or irritated eyes.
side_effects: Brief stinging or blurred vision; preservative sensitivity with frequent use.
extra_information: Lubricating drops ease dryness but do not treat every cause of red or painful eyes. Wash hands and avoid touching the bottle tip to the eye. Severe pain, light sensitivity, injury, vision change or contact-lens-related redness needs prompt assessment.

name: Dicyclomine
uses: Certain intestinal spasms or cramps when a clinician recommends it.
side_effects: Dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, constipation, difficulty urinating.
extra_information: An antispasmodic that may not be suitable for glaucoma, urinary retention, bowel obstruction or some older adults. Combination brands may contain additional ingredients, so check the label. Severe or persistent abdominal pain, fever, blood in stool or vomiting needs medical assessment.

name: Melatonin
uses: Selected sleep-timing problems under appropriate guidance; availability and regulation vary.
side_effects: Sleepiness, headache, dizziness, vivid dreams.
extra_information: Can cause next-day drowsiness and interact with sedatives or other medicines. Avoid driving if sleepy and check suitability for pregnancy, chronic illness or regular use with a clinician. Persistent insomnia may have an underlying cause that needs assessment.

name: Nicotine Replacement Therapy (Nicotine Gum/Patch)
uses: Support for quitting smoking when used according to product guidance.
side_effects: Gum: jaw or mouth irritation, hiccups; patch: skin irritation or sleep disturbance.
extra_information: Provides nicotine without cigarette smoke and can reduce withdrawal symptoms. Choose the product and strength with a pharmacist or clinician, especially in pregnancy or with recent serious heart problems. Avoid smoking while using it unless a clinician has given a specific plan.

name: Emergency Contraceptive Levonorgestrel
uses: Emergency contraception after unprotected sex or contraceptive failure.
side_effects: Nausea, headache, fatigue, cramps, spotting or a shifted next period.
extra_information: Works best when taken as soon as possible within the product’s recommended time window; it does not end an established pregnancy and does not protect against sexually transmitted infections or later sex. Take a pregnancy test or seek advice if the period is significantly late or symptoms concern you.

name: Clopidogrel
uses: Prevention of blood clots after certain heart attacks, strokes, stents or vascular conditions.
side_effects: Bruising, nosebleeds, bleeding; rarely serious bleeding or blood disorders.
extra_information: An antiplatelet medicine that reduces clot formation. Do not stop it without the prescribing clinician’s advice, particularly after a coronary stent. Tell healthcare professionals before surgery and ask before using NSAIDs because bleeding risk can rise.

name: Aspirin (Low-Dose Antiplatelet)
uses: Prevention of cardiovascular events in selected people when prescribed.
side_effects: Stomach irritation, ulcers, bleeding, bruising; allergy or asthma worsening in some people.
extra_information: Low-dose aspirin is not appropriate for everyone and should not be started routinely for prevention without clinician advice. It increases bleeding risk; do not combine with other blood thinners or NSAIDs without guidance. Seek urgent care for black stools or vomiting blood.
